  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

The Brewers own a massive division lead but the Pirates have quietly been their kryptonite lately, and this game pairs two of the more electric young arms in the league. Jared Jones just came back from a two-month injured-list stint and has rediscovered his stuff in July, posting a 2.00 ERA over five starts, and his velocity (98.5 mph average, a huge z-score outlier) and elite xFIP- back it up—hence a hearty 9.82 pNERD. Across from him, Logan Henderson has been arguably better on the ledger sheet, running a minuscule 70 xFIP- with a strong strikeout rate that lands him at 9.78 pNERD, continuing an 8-1 career run that includes a scoreless outing against the Giants his last time out. On the team side, Milwaukee's 9.17 tNERD is buoyed by a deep, young roster with strong baserunning and bullpen numbers, while Pittsburgh's 6.93 isn't far behind thanks to solid batting and baserunning of their own—fitting, given they've won four straight against the Brewers, including Monday's 4-3 series-opening upset. Add it up and you get a 17.85 gNERD, comfortably above both the historical and today's averages—this one's worth your evening.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

Skubal traded to the Dodgers, making his debut against a lineup that isn't even his old team — that's the headline here, and it's a legitimately fun watch. This is Tarik Skubal's first start as a Dodger, coming to Wrigley just days after L.A. sent a package to Detroit to get him, and his 12.51 pNERD says the hype is earned. His shiny surface stats undersell it: Skubal carries a 31.0% strikeout rate with just a 3.7% walk rate this season, and his 0.910 WHIP ranks among the best in baseball, and his swinging-strike and strike-rate z-scores are near the top of the league, backed by a stingy xFIP-. He's also been on a run before the trade — in his past six outings, Skubal has given up only eight earned runs in 37 innings for an ERA of 1.95 — so this isn't just name value. Assad is a solid, unspectacular caretaker in the back half of the rotation with a low swinging-strike rate that drags his pNERD to a modest 2.75, and the Cubs are missing several top arms this series, which only widens the pitching gap. Both offenses carry real thump, though: the Dodgers' bat-heavy, deep lineup and a Cubs defense with an outstanding fielding number both push their tNERDs near 9.3, among the best pairings you'll see today or in the wider dataset, and Wrigley Field adds ambiance to a gNERD score (16.90) that ranks near the top of the pack.

St. Louis Cardinals @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Good, this gives me enough to work with. Let me write the summary.

This series opener slugfest sequel has real upside: the Yankees are chasing a bounce-back after Monday's wild 13-7 loss where Alec Burleson hit three homers off them, and Tuesday brings a legitimately compelling pitching matchup to boot. Ryan Weathers, the Yankees' lefty, owns the better peripherals here — his 79 xFIP- and 8.36 pNERD suggest he's pitching better than his 3.99 ERA lets on, and he's actually been a bit unlucky, so there's more in the tank than the raw numbers show. Hunter Dobbins, back from an ACL tear that ended his Red Sox tenure and now starting for St. Louis after the offseason trade for Willson Contreras, brings a solid 6.00 pNERD and a lively 95-plus mph fastball. New York's lineup is banged up — Aaron Judge (rib), Giancarlo Stanton (leg), and Cody Bellinger (leg) are all out — but the Yankees still post an 8.07 tNERD thanks to elite barrel rates and a deep bullpen, comfortably above both the historic and today's-game averages. Add in a Cardinals offense that just dropped 13 runs on this same pitching staff, and the 13.95 gNERD checks out: this one lands well above the historic median and near the top of today's slate.

Washington Nationals @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Good enough info to write the summary.

Jesús Luzardo brings swing-and-miss stuff and a Nationals lineup that's mashing everything not named Luzardo, making this the rare Nats-Phillies game worth clearing your schedule for. Luzardo carries a strikeout rate near 29% and a tidy 3.57 ERA into the outing, though he's looking to bounce back from allowing six runs in 6.1 innings to the Marlins last time out, after allowing just eight earned runs in 49.1 innings across his previous eight starts. His pNERD of 10.58 backs that up — well above the 95th percentile for today's games — thanks to a strong xFIP-, plush velocity, and a bit of positive regression coming his way. Littell, by contrast, is scuffling for a Washington rotation gutted by injuries; the Nationals have DJ Herz, Josiah Gray, Mitchell Parker, Ken Waldichuk, and Connelly Early all on the injured list, leaving the club relying heavily on Littell despite his 5.94 FIP and negative WAR. That mismatch drags the pitching side down, but Washington's offense — young, athletic, and running wild on the bases — pushes the Nationals' tNERD to 9.24, comfortably above the historic 95th percentile. Philadelphia's bullpen depth and broadcast ratings add just enough polish to make the 13.19 gNERD a solidly above-average watch.

Chicago White Sox @ Boston Red Sox, 4:10p

Summary

Surprising things brewing in Chicago: the White Sox sit atop the AL Central by three games and just added Luis Castillo at the deadline, while the Red Sox went the other direction, spending big to land catcher Adley Rutschman (though he's currently shelved with wrist inflammation). Watch for a lineup boasting Colson Montgomery's power numbers against a Sandoval who has been shaky historically versus Chicago.

Worth a look mostly for the standings drama, not the pitching matchup. The White Sox (8.37 tNERD) bring real thump and a deep bullpen while somehow running one of the game's youngest, cheapest rosters — a nice underdog profile for a team clinging to a division lead. Boston's tNERD (5.86) is more modest, buoyed by strong glovework and relief work but dragged by so-so contact quality. On the mound, Davis Martin's strong underlying numbers (3.11 FIP, 0.54 HR/9) make him more interesting than his recent results suggest, even as backs pages call him homer-prone. Patrick Sandoval, still building back innings and grading out with essentially no track record yet in our pNERD model, is the wildcard — he's 0-3 with a 6.41 ERA in four career starts against the White Sox, including a 2-1 win in his Red Sox debut on July 9. Overall, a 12.30 gNERD lands comfortably above the historical average, thanks more to the teams than the arms.

Miami Marlins @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

I now have enough for a solid summary.

Miami's low-payroll, high-baserunning Marlins bring some genuine juice into Truist Park, even if Vegas thinks this is a laugher waiting to happen. The Braves are the far bigger name here, but the Marlins actually carry the better tNERD (9.82 to 6.31), fueled by a recovery from a franchise-record 12-game losing streak to win six of seven, including three straight against the New York Mets, plus a young, cheap roster that's been running better than its underlying luck number suggests. Atlanta counters with its own hot streak — riding a five-game winning streak after going 12-5 since the All-Star break, including a four-game weekend sweep over the Washington Nationals — but its tNERD gets docked for negative batted-luck and an older, pricier roster that doesn't get bonus points here. On the mound, Ryan Gusto (pNERD 5.12) is scuffling on the surface — 0-2 with a 5.31 ERA and 1.44 WHIP — but his underlying numbers and tough luck number suggest better days ahead. Grant Holmes (pNERD 2.99) is the steadier stat-line arm at 6-4, 3.88 ERA, 1.36 WHIP, though he gave up a season-high three home runs in his last outing against the Nationals. The 12.13 gNERD lands a bit above the historical average, mostly on the strength of Miami's team profile rather than a marquee pitching duel.

New York Mets @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

Sean Manaea takes the mound for a Mets team stuck deep in the NL East cellar—a matchup between a struggling road club and a Cleveland team that just made trade-deadline reinforcements, though nothing here screams must-watch. The Mets have lost three of their last four and lost three in a row and four of their last five after winning three straight, scoring just four runs in their last three games, while Cleveland has struggled recently as well, but got some reinforcements at the trade deadline on Monday. Manaea has been trending the right way, though: after a rough start to July, he finished strong allowing three runs in 12 innings over his last two starts, and his pNERD of 5.18 reflects an average-ish profile boosted by a slow pace and some positive regression luck. Cantillo, meanwhile, is the steadier arm of the two—his most recent start was four shutout innings against Cincinnati, a bounce-back from two rough outings that saw him give up 15 hits and nine runs over 8.2 innings—and his 5.43 pNERD edges Manaea's slightly on the back of a strong swinging-strike rate. Cleveland's tNERD (7.27) comfortably outpaces the Mets' (4.73), thanks to a young, cheap roster that grades out well on baserunning and payroll efficiency. The 11.30 gNERD lands almost exactly at today's average, so treat this as a solid midweek option rather than a can't-miss.

San Francisco Giants @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

This one's mostly a showcase for MacKenzie Gore, since the Giants side of the roster is running on fumes after a deadline sell-off. Gore brings real stuff to the mound — mid-90s velocity, a healthy whiff rate, and an xFIP- of 93 that suggests he's been pitching better than his results, with some positive regression likely coming given his underperforming luck number. Opposite him is Blade Tidwell, who makes his first start of the season for San Francisco, so there's zero pNERD data to lean on and plenty of uncertainty about what shows up. The Giants, at 47-65, have sold at the deadline and effectively conceded that this is not their year, though the offense has picked up lately, while Texas has actually been scuffling and getting shut out. Both clubs carry outsized positive luck scores, meaning the underlying numbers say better days are ahead for each. The gNERD of 11.04 sits a tick above the historical average and roughly in the middle of today's slate — watchable mainly for Gore, less so for anything resembling playoff stakes.

A former Twins washout is quietly outdueling his old team's ace, and that oddity alone makes this worth a glance — even if the underlying NERD math says skip it. Kansas City's Randy Dobnak, who was designated for assignment and bounced to the Mariners before Kansas City picked him up, has been the story of this series: Dobnak, the longtime Twin who was acquired by Kansas City from Seattle in June, has been outstanding since his debut with the Royals on July 2. Just last Wednesday he tossed seven shutout innings against his former club, permitting four hits and one walk in seven innings while striking out four, matching a career high and marking the first time he'd thrown more than 100 pitches in a start. Joe Ryan, meanwhile, is scuffling — he's 1-4 with a 4.91 ERA over his last six starts, allowing 12 runs and 18 hits in 10 innings of the past two — though his xFIP- of 87 still says he's the better bet on paper, and he owns this game's only pitcher NERD score of note (6.23) thanks to strong strike-throwing and whiff rates. Dobnak's pNERD (3.14) is a mirage built on a tidy ERA rather than real stuff. Team-wise, both clubs are duds: Minnesota's bullpen and defense are dragging its tNERD to 2.73, and Kansas City's bullpen (-36.5 runs) is arguably the worst in the league, propping up its 3.01 mark only via positive luck. Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

This one has real juice: two 60-plus-win rivals, elite defenses, and a Cubs offense trying to snap out of a funk against a Dodgers club nursing a bruised ego after getting swept by Boston. The gNERD of 14.45 sits well above both the historical average (10.11) and today's slate (10.80), driven almost entirely by two outstanding team profiles — Dodgers (9.41) and Cubs (9.31) both rank near the top of the historic tNERD distribution, fueled by strong batting runs and, in the Cubs' case, an absurd fielding-runs mark of 55.6. The Dodgers arrive looking to reset after Dave Roberts admitted "They outplayed us" in a series where Boston outscored Los Angeles 20-10 over the three games, costing them the best record in baseball. Matthew Boyd (5.19 pNERD, solid strike-throwing and respectable xFIP-) takes the mound for Chicago, while the Dodgers' listed TBD starter is actually expected to be Justin Wrobleski, who enters with a 2.88 ERA over 112.2 IP despite peripherals suggesting he's been pretty lucky this year. Add in a Cubs bullpen that's shaky and a Dodgers pen anchored by a bounced-back Tanner Scott, and this is a legitimately watchable ballgame.

St. Louis Cardinals @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Cam Schlittler's electric arm makes this one worth catching, even if the Cardinals side of the ledger looks bleak. This is Schlittler's Cy Young-caliber season on display — the right-hander carries a 2.04 ERA and has struck out 165 batters this season, backed by a blistering four-seam fastball that sits at 97.9 mph and generates a 30.4% whiff rate with a .234 xwOBA against. His pNERD of 10.54 is comfortably above today's average and sits near the top of the historical distribution, fueled by elite strikeout stuff and top-shelf velocity. McGreevy, by contrast, is scuffling badly — his last outing saw him come against the Cubs on July 28, one of the roughest starts of his season, lasting only 1⅔ innings while allowing seven earned runs — and his 3.67 pNERD reflects thin whiff and strike-rate numbers. The Yankees' 8.16 tNERD, boosted by strong barrel rate and baserunning marks, dwarfs a punchless Cardinals lineup dealing with a slump; St. Louis has fallen under .500 with seven losses in their last 10 games and sits four games out of the final wild card spot. New York is banged up too, with Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, and Carlos Rodón all on the injured list, but that hardly dents this gNERD of 13.82, which lands well above both the historical and today's averages — mostly on the strength of one dominant arm.

Team-wise, the Brewers' 9.18 tNERD is elite - built on baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young roster - while Pittsburgh's 7.05 isn't far behind. entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Los Angeles Angels, 12:15p

Summary

This is the day's marquee pitching matchup, and it's not particularly close. Jacob Misiorowski takes the mound fresh off a start where he struck out the first seven Rockies batters to set a Brewers franchise record, then retired the first 14 hitters he faced before a two-out homer in the fifth, and he's doing it while setting a pitch-tracking-era record by throwing all 66 of his fastballs at least 100 mph. His 15.66 pNERD is comfortably the best of any pitcher in today's slate, built on elite whiff rates, a sub-50 xFIP-, and velocity that sits near the top of the league — this is a legitimate NL Cy Young caliber arm. Walbert Ureña isn't chopped liver either, pairing a mid-90s-plus fastball with a 6.46 pNERD, though he leans on that heater more than most (over half his pitches) and his strikeout rate looks a bit lucky. On the team side, Milwaukee's 9.42 tNERD (young, athletic, good bullpen) dwarfs a last-place Angels club (1.19 tNERD) currently on a five-game skid with the majors' worst record. Historically this game's 16.37 gNERD ranks near the top of the distribution — well above today's 11.26 average — making it the pick of the day almost entirely on Misiorowski's arm.

Boston Red Sox @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 4:20p

Summary

A rookie sensation with a clean fastball meets a homer-prone but swing-and-miss righty in a Dodger Stadium series finale that's more compelling than the standings gap suggests. Boston's Jake Bennett, a 6-foot-6 southpaw acquired from the Nationals, has emerged in a big way after posting a 1.60 ERA at Triple-A before getting the call, and he's allowed three or fewer runs in each of his last eight starts — his pNERD of 7.02 reflects strong control and a favorable age curve for a rookie still finding his ceiling. Emmet Sheehan counters with real strikeout stuff (a 27.4% K% this year, placing in the 88th percentile) but has been homer-prone all year, and his positive luck component suggests his ugly ERA should trend better than his surface numbers indicate. The Dodgers' offense is the headline attraction here, ranking near the top of MLB in several categories and pushing their tNERD to 9.49 — comfortably above today's average — while the lineup ranks first in the majors in batting average at .262. Add in Boston's playoff urgency against a Dodgers club coasting toward October, and this 14.47 gNERD sits well above both the historical and today's averages, making it one of the day's better watches.

Overall gNERD of 10.44 lands almost exactly at the historical median - a decent, not thrilling, way to spend an afternoon, buoyed almost entirely by two arms worth watching.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Boston Red Sox @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

I have enough information from my searches to write a well-supported summary.

Payton Tolle's first look at a Dodgers lineup loaded with October ghosts is the story here, and the Dodgers' star-studded roster combined with a legitimate pitching duel makes this one of the day's better watches. Tolle, Boston's former second-round pick and top pitching prospect, made his major-league debut just last summer against Paul Skenes and the Pirates, and this outing gives fans a chance to see the 23-year-old lefty—armed with elite extension and a five-pitch mix—test himself against a genuine championship-caliber lineup rather than a rebuilding club.A rookie fireballer taking on a stacked Dodgers lineup, in a game that ranks near the top of the day's watchability charts—this one's worth clearing your schedule for. The gNERD of 16.18 sits comfortably above both today's average (11.35) and the historic norm (10.11), driven largely by the Dodgers' tNERD of 9.48, one of the stronger offensive-and-defensive packages you'll see, powered by elite batting runs and a barrel rate that would make any pitcher nervous. Boston's 5.86 tNERD is more middling, propped up by a strong bullpen and a bit of positive luck suggesting they've actually underperformed their true talent level.

On the mound, Payton Tolle, the Red Sox's second-round pick out of TCU, was ranked as the team's No. 2 prospect, compiling a 3.44 ERA with 133 strikeouts in 91 2/3 innings before rocketing to the majors. His pNERD of 9.06 reflects excellent strike-throwing and swinging-strike marks for a 23-year-old with mid-90s velocity. Yamamoto counters with a 7.95 pNERD, anchored by a sparkling 79 xFIP-, making this a legitimately compelling pitching matchup wrapped around a lopsided but entertaining lineup mismatch.

entry.content:

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:10p

Summary

Two of the best arms in baseball facing off means this one's a must-watch, even if the box scores haven't been kind to one of them. This game's 17.34 gNERD sits near the top of both today's slate (average 11.09) and the historical distribution (95th percentile is 14.76), and the pitching matchup is the reason why. Paul Skenes brings his usual excellence — a 2.72 FIP, 30.4% strikeout rate, and only a 5.7% walk rate this season — and has been particularly nasty against Cincinnati, owning a 5-0 record with a 1.38 ERA, 52 strikeouts and six walks over 39 innings in his career against the Reds. Hunter Greene's actual pNERD-topping 12.25 tells a different story than his ugly 7.06 ERA suggests: his underlying peripherals (3.20 FIP, 3.09 xFIP) suggest his results have been far worse than his stuff, a classic case of bad luck (and a return from an early-season elbow injury) masking real swing-and-miss ability. The Reds' offense has been genuinely poor this year, dragging their tNERD down, while the Pirates counter with solid baserunning and pop but shaky defense. Elly De La Cruz has been a standout at home, hitting .320 with a .970 OPS and 10 home runs in 172 at-bats at Great American Ball Park, giving Skenes at least one dangerous bat to navigate.

New York Yankees @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Good stuff — plenty of storylines here. Let me write the summary.

A Wrigley Field matinee with real fielding wizardry and an offense-vs-lefty-with-a-barrel-problem subplot makes this the most watchable game on the board today. Both tNERD marks are near the top of what we've seen this year — the Cubs' 9.23 is boosted by elite team defense (fielding runs cratering z-scores at 3.10) and a strong batting attack, while the Yankees check in at 8.54 thanks to raw power (top-tier barrel rate) and baserunning value, even while missing Aaron Judge, who landed on the 60-day injured list with a rib injury and, as of the latest team updates, was still working through scans before resuming baseball activities, plus Cody Bellinger and Giancarlo Stanton. Imanaga is the headliner on the mound, a lefty who has a 1.10 WHIP that dwarfs Will Warren's 1.41, and who's coming off an outstanding July, posting a 1.19 ERA across four starts, including back-to-back scoreless outings. Warren, by contrast, has been rough lately — allowing six earned runs in three innings in his last outing, part of a subpar July where he's 0-2 with a 7.50 ERA — though his xFIP still checks out fine underneath the noise. Pete Crow-Armstrong versus a shorthanded Yankees lineup is worth watching too.

If you tune in, it's for Coors Field trivia and the fun quirks in the box score, not for stakes or aces.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

A first-place showdown with a red-hot White Sox ace and a fading Yankees lineup down to its studs — this one has drama even if the box score might not be pretty for New York. Chicago sits atop the AL Central and gets a huge boost from Sean Burke, who has been red hot as of late, posting a 1.61 ERA since his last start against New York in mid-June, backing up his solid 6.66 pNERD with a tidy xFIP- of 89. Ryan Weathers actually rates a touch higher on pure stuff (8.84 pNERD, xFIP- of 77), but Weathers's last five starts have produced an ERA of 5.5, and he's without some serious offensive help — Aaron Judge is out, Giancarlo Stanton is out, Cody Bellinger is out. Both clubs carry matching 8.48-8.49 tNERD scores, with the White Sox's youthful, discount-payroll roster and the Yankees' power/baserunning combo each pulling real weight. With a 16.24 gNERD, this game ranks well above both the historical median and today's slate average, making it one of the stronger watches on the board. Add a tight division race and a lopsided season head-to-head — Yankees are 4-2 against Chicago this year — and there's plenty of subplot even before the first pitch.

Miami Marlins @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

A rookie phenom with elite stuff against a hard-throwing 23-year-old Marlins arm, wrapped around a Miami team that just snapped a 12-game losing streak in dramatic fashion — this one's worth your evening. Nolan McLean has been arguably the Mets' best story of the season, carrying a 79 xFIP- and a 2.17 ERA in 58.0 innings over his last 10 starts dating back to May 31, and his 8.61 pNERD reflects a genuinely dominant, young power arm. Eury Pérez counters with 98-mph heat and a well above-average swinging-strike rate, giving this game two of the more compelling starters you'll see on a given day. Miami arrives with real juice: after setting a franchise record with 12 consecutive losses, Miami has rattled off three straight wins to stabilize, including a dominant stretch against Philadelphia that featured Sandy Alcantara's return to form and late-game heroics from Griffin Conine. The Marlins' 9.84 tNERD is buoyed by strong baserunning and a favorable luck score suggesting more contention ahead, while the Mets, missing Juan Soto and Mark Vientos to injury, limp in with a middling offense. Combined, the 15.39 gNERD sits well above both the historical average and today's slate, making this one of the sharper watches on the board.

Seattle Mariners @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered so far, since I have solid material on Sasaki and the Dodgers/Mariners context.

A juicy pitching duel with two of the game's most electric arms, even if one of them is still finding his footing. Roki Sasaki brings triple-digit stuff and a season of turbulence to Dodger Stadium, while Bryan Woo quietly continues to be one of the more efficient strike-throwers in the league — this is a game where the gNERD score of 14.40 sits well above both the historical average (10.11) and even today's slate average (11.63), and it shows.

Sasaki's command has been shaky since returning to the rotation, with 69 hits and 38 walks in 70 innings and his ERA climbing to 5.88 in seven starts this year. He's even dealt with a start against San Diego where the opposition seemed to be sitting on everything he threw, though his velocity remains elite — his 97.8 mph average sits well above league norms and drives most of his 8.25 pNERD. Woo, by contrast, is a model of efficiency: his strike-throwing and command (73rd-percentile strike rate, low walk totals) push his pNERD to 7.93 despite modest raw stuff, and he's currently running well ahead of his peripherals on the luck front, suggesting some regression toward even better results isn't out of the question. On the team side, the Dodgers' 9.52 tNERD is elite, built on top-tier batting runs and barrel rate, while Seattle's 3.11 is closer to replacement level — so expect fireworks from the lineup wearing blue.

Washington Nationals @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Jake Irvin's return from a two-month shoulder absence is the real hook here, and it comes with a twist of dramatic irony: he tore up his shoulder in this very matchup back in May, mid-way through a hitless outing against Atlanta. He's back for the rematch, and while his pNERD (4.80) is unspectacular, the storyline carries real weight. Grant Holmes, meanwhile, has been a solid performer in both starts since returning from the All-Star break, and his last outing extended a streak to 13 straight appearances allowing three or fewer runs—steady if not electric, reflected in his modest 3.00 pNERD.

The offense is where this game earns its 11.66 gNERD, roughly average for today's slate but comfortably above the historical median. Washington's lineup is the story of the year in Washington: the Nationals lead MLB with 596 runs scored and 159 home runs as we approach August, fueled by James Wood and CJ Abrams, and that shows up in Washington's excellent 9.41 tNERD—elite batting and baserunning marks offset by a genuinely bad bullpen. Atlanta counters as the division's top dog, comfortably perched atop the NL East with a 6½-game lead over the Phillies, though missing Acuña and several arms. Good lineups, shaky pens—expect some fireworks, if not artistry.

The Cubs bring the far superior roster here, with elite fielding and a lineup carried by Crow-Armstrong, who's quietly built a season with 24 home runs, 26 stolen bases, and 71 runs scored that makes him must-watch even when the arms on the mound aren't. Chicago's defense and bat-driven tNERD dwarfs a scuffling Cardinals offense that's been genuinely unlucky underperforming its peripherals — a mild positive for St. Louis's outlook, even if it hasn't shown up in the standings yet.

The pitching matchup is the softer part of the equation. Detail

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Highest gNERD score on the board today, and this one earns it on pure quality rather than randomness. Cam Schlittler is the story here—the AL ERA leader is fresh off a 7⅓-inning shutout gem against Philadelphia with 12 strikeouts, and his a 1.48 ERA in May swelled to 3.38 in June before he returned to form in July with a 2.05 ERA in four starts. His 10.44 pNERD is elite, driven by a filthy 97.8 mph average fastball, a stingy xFIP-, and an eye-popping strikeout rate; Paul Goldschmidt even floated Cy Young talk. Davis Martin is no slouch either, with a respectable 5.29 pNERD backed by strong contact management, though he's had a rough go over the last 30 days, with his poor underlying numbers suggesting the results are warranted. Both teams carry nearly identical tNERD scores in the 8.5-8.6 range—well above the historical 95th percentile of 8.60—thanks to Chicago's young, cheap roster and New York's power-and-speed combo. The White Sox arrive having lost four of five yet still atop the AL Central, while the Yankees are missing Judge, Stanton, and Bellinger but have still won this series' first two games. A well-rounded, watchable matchup all around.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 9:10a

Summary

Luzardo torching his old team headlines a game that ranks near the top of today's slate for watchability, even if the Marlins' offense figures to be mostly a bystander. Luzardo, an All-Star this year, carries a 10.56 pNERD into Miami, and the numbers back up the eye test: he's not allowed more than one earned run in any of his last six games, has struck out six or more in each, and he's already torched the Marlins, posting nine-plus strikeouts over six innings and allowing just two runs in his first two meetings with Miami this season. His xFIP- of 69 and 96.6 mph average velocity explain the strong pNERD, and a modest positive luck figure suggests even his gaudy numbers haven't fully caught up to his stuff. Gusto, by contrast, is a replacement-level type (4.19 pNERD) who's been alternating between the bullpen and rotation since being called up from Triple-A Jacksonville in early June. The Marlins' 9.83 tNERD is buoyed by a young, cheap roster and a hot streak of racing around the bases with Otto Lopez, currently drawing trade buzz, leading the majors in batting average. Philadelphia, meanwhile, is scuffling and has fallen further back in the NL East. Not a great pitching matchup on paper, but Luzardo alone makes it worth a look.

Baltimore Orioles @ Detroit Tigers, 10:10a

Great, this is exactly what I needed - a dramatic result. Let me write the summary now.

Tarik Skubal's likely farewell start in a Tigers uniform turned into an instant classic, and this recap captures why the whole night was must-watch. With the Aug. 3 trade deadline looming and Detroit lingering under .500, this was billed as Skubal's most anticipated outing—possibly his final start as a Detroit Tiger, as the trade deadline draws closer and the Tigers remain mired in the playoff race. He delivered a milestone moment, too: Skubal got his first standing ovation when he struck out leadoff hitter Taylor Ward on a 3-2 changeup to record his 1,000th career strikeout, then tipped his cap to the fans. But the story didn't end there—Skubal was taking a 7-0 shutout into the seventh inning against Baltimore, but then the Orioles rallied from a 7-0 deficit to beat Detroit 10-9 in 12 innings.

The NERD numbers back up the hype: this game's 13.37 gNERD sits comfortably above the historic average of 10.11, and well above today's slate average too. Skubal's 12.86 pNERD is elite—driven by a filthy 58 xFIP-, top-shelf swinging-strike and strike rates, and mid-90s-plus velocity—while Trevor Rogers is merely average opposite him. Both bullpens and lineups are middling by tNERD, but none of that matters once Skubal starts humming; just don't expect a shutout given how the last meeting between these two clubs went.

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

This one's near the top of the watchability charts today, and deservedly so: a red-hot Brewers club with a dominant bullpen taking on a Giants team that keeps overachieving its underlying numbers. Milwaukee sits atop the NL Central at 66-40 after a strong homestand, bringing the show to Old Friend Willy Adames and the Giants to open a West Coast trip — a nice subplot given Adames spent years anchoring Milwaukee's infield before signing in San Francisco. The Brewers' 9.00 tNERD is driven by an excellent bullpen, quality baserunning, and a young, cheap roster, while the Giants' still-solid 4.66 mark leans heavily on Oracle Park broadcast charm and a notable "positive luck" gap — meaning San Francisco (45-61) has actually been playing worse than its record indicates. On the mound, 24-year-old Logan Henderson is the headliner, with a 4-1 record, 3.05 ERA, 0.94 WHIP and elite peripherals (9.92 pNERD, well above today's 5.78 average) built on excellent strike-throwing and whiff rates. Landen Roupp counters capably, with a 7-8 record, 3.93 ERA, and 113 strikeouts, giving this game a legitimately compelling top-of-scale gNERD of 15.00.

A frontline arm carrying a middling supporting cast is the story here, with Cleveland's Gavin Williams doing enough heavy lifting to make this one worth your remote. Williams' pNERD of 11.50 sits near the top of both today's slate and the broader season sample, built on a hard-to-square combination of premium velocity (97 mph average) and elite contact suppression (xFIP- of 72). The Reds' counterpart is officially unnamed, which is its own small mystery, though Cincinnati's lineup gives him little help either way — Cincinnati's tNERD of 4.11 reflects a club with shaky batting and fielding runs, and they'll be doing it without Steer, who's headed for the injured list after a right wrist injury expected to cost "significant time". Cleveland's offense isn't exactly thriving either — the Guardians have been shut out in their last two games and scored just four runs in their last four — but their 7.16 tNERD, boosted by strong baserunning and bullpen work, still clears the Reds comfortably. Not a marquee slugfest, but Williams alone makes this worth checking in on.

Nola is in the middle of the worst season of his career, having allowed more home runs (25) than any pitcher in the National League this season, though his pNERD (5.16) gets a boost from positive luck, suggesting his ugly ERA overstates how bad he's been. Overall, at 7.04 the gNERD sits below both the historical and today's-slate averages — watch for Detmers, not much else.

Detail

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Zack Wheeler is quietly having one of the better seasons in baseball and Miami is in full collapse mode—that combination makes this worth your evening. The Marlins have dropped 12 straight games, a franchise record, and have yet to win since the All-Star break. Wheeler counters that misery by walking in with a sparkling 10-2 record and a 2.16 ERA, backed by an xFIP- of just 65 and elite swinging-strike rate that push his pNERD to 9.09, comfortably above today's average. Tyler Phillips is a serviceable but unspectacular foil — decent velocity, shaky command, a 110 xFIP- — giving this matchup a real talent gap on the mound, even if the raw box score (2-5, 3.52 ERA) undersells how rough his peripherals have been. On the offensive side, Philadelphia's lineup can erupt (Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber's 33 homers lead the way) though the Phillies own tNERD is middling due to underwhelming batting runs. Miami, despite the losing streak, posts a strong 9.62 tNERD thanks to speed, a young roster, and bad luck that suggests better days ahead — Otto Lopez's .328 average and Xavier Edwards' on-base ability keep the bottom-feeder lineup from being a total non-factor. With a 14.03 gNERD, this sits near the top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average.

Cleveland Guardians @ Cincinnati Reds, 4:10p

Summary

Chase Burns is the whole show here, and he's making Cincinnati's mediocre roster look like a contender every fifth day. Cleveland's Guardians arrive with a lineup that grinds out at-bats but not much thunder, while Cincinnati counters with a rookie who's rapidly becoming must-watch television.

Burns, just 23, comes in at 12-1 with a 2.42 ERA, and he'll take the mound for the Reds in his 20th start of the season, coming off a start where he allowed three hits in five scoreless innings against Seattle. His 2.42 ERA and 10.4 strikeouts per nine with a .204 batting average against back up a pNERD of 9.83 — miles above today's average and squarely elite territory, fueled by nearly-98 mph heat and a swinging-strike rate that makes hitters look silly. He's also fresh off signing a seven-year, $105 million extension, so no shortage of stakes here. Cecconi, opposite him, is a stark contrast: a 4-7, 4.60 ERA innings-eater with an ordinary 3.28 pNERD, though his last start against Minnesota (4⅔ innings, three earned runs) wasn't inspiring. Cleveland's tNERD (7.25) actually outpaces Cincinnati's (4.18), thanks to bullpen depth, youth, and baserunning value, while the Reds lean on raw barrel rate and a bit of positive batting luck. Overall gNERD of 12.27 sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — watch it for Burns alone.

Boston Red Sox @ Athletics, 6:40p

Summary

Boston's playing spoiler in Sacramento against a team that's basically imploding, and the pitching matchup is the reason to tune in even if the rest of the game plot is thin. The Athletics are riding an ugly stretch — just three wins in their last ten — and things got worse with news that the Athletics could learn Monday that All-Star catcher Shea Langeliers requires season-ending knee surgery. Boston, by contrast, has won six consecutive series for the first time since June 2022 and enters riding an 8-of-10 stretch. The pitching is the real draw: 23-year-old lefty Payton Tolle owns the second-highest pNERD among today's starters, thanks to elite strike-throwing, a quick pace, and mid-90s velocity, backed by a .206 xBA against, .267 xwOBA, and a strikeout rate near 27% with a chase rate over 34%. Perkins isn't far behind on stuff, though his surface numbers (6.75 ERA) lag his peripherals. Boston's tNERD gets a lift from strong fielding and bullpen work; Oakland's suffers from shaky defense and baserunning, offset partly by youth and payroll scarcity. At 12.23, this gNERD sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — a solid, if not spectacular, watch.

Chicago Cubs @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 10:35a

Summary

A dominant Ashcraft strikeout arm meets a Cubs offense riding a 31-run scoring binge, making this the day's most watchable matchup on paper. At 15.67, today's gNERD sits well above both the historic average (10.11) and today's slate average (11.32), and it's driven mostly by a lopsided pitching matchup: Braxton Ashcraft's 11.58 pNERD (elite xFIP-, 97 mph heat, brisk pace) dwarfs Jameson Taillon's modest 3.97. That said, Ashcraft's last outing saw him give up seven earned runs in three innings against the Yankees, so buyer beware on recent form even as his skills grade out well. The Pirates enter having Pittsburgh hosting the Cubs while riding a three-game losing skid and are trying to avoid a series sweep. Both offenses carry real juice—Chicago's tNERD (8.49) and Pittsburgh's (7.30) both rank comfortably above the historic 75th percentile—with Pete Crow-Armstrong pacing Chicago in OBP (.390) and slugging (.544) and Bryan Reynolds anchoring Pittsburgh. Add in Taillon's history as a former Pirate first-round product returning to PNC Park, and there's enough juice here to make this the pick of the day.

Misiorowski, the 24-year-old flamethrower who's become a genuine Cy Young conversation piece, leads the majors with 173 strikeouts and in ERA, and he consistently hits 100 mph or more on the radar gun. His pNERD of 15.00 is essentially maxed out, driven by elite whiff rates, a microscopic xFIP-, and velocity that sits near the top of the league — this is as close to appointment viewing as a start gets. Opposite him, Kyle Freeland has been scuffling, having lost his last two decisions, allowing four runs over six innings in both outings, though his pNERD of 5.37 is respectable thanks to strong control and some rough luck. The Brewers' 8.87 tNERD (driven by baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young, boosted lineup) dwarfs Colorado's league-worst 1.41, with Milwaukee's rookies Cooper Pratt and Luis Lara instrumental in Saturday night's 8-5 Milwaukee win. New York Yankees @ Philadelphia Phillies, 4:20p

Summary

I've got enough to write a solid summary now.

Watch this one for Sánchez alone — a legitimate Cy Young-caliber arm against a Yankees lineup that leads baseball in team ERA, with the Phillies trying to snap a home skid. Cristopher Sánchez brings a 10.21 pNERD, driven by an absurd 61 xFIP-, elite swinging-strike rate, and plus velocity — this is a top-shelf starter having a genuinely dominant season. This is his 22nd start of the season, and the 29-year-old carries a 2.65 ERA with a 6.04 strikeout-to-walk ratio. That said, July has been rough for him, with a 7.47 ERA and 1.98 WHIP across 16 innings, plus a jump in barrel rate — worth watching whether he's settling back in. Opposite him, Will Warren (4.33 pNERD) is a more pedestrian arm, prone to traffic on the bases, though he's shown flashes of getting outs when it matters. The Yankees' 8.54 tNERD is the headline offensive story here — strong barrel rates, baserunning, and bullpen — while Philadelphia's 5.34 leans more on baserunning and pen depth than its middling bat. Philadelphia sits at 27-27 at home and 38-5 when scoring five-plus runs, so a quiet Phillies bat could make this lopsided fast. At 14.21 gNERD, this ranks comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — a good pick.
